records.summary: 895 O'Farrell St is zoned NCD-Lower Polk Street where a restaurant is principally permitted on the first story. The records show no prior applications or ABC licenses at this exact address or parcel (0717/013), so the existing use is not established by the public record. The immediate area is densely served: 25 registered food/drink businesses within 500 ft, 6 active ABC on-sale licenses within 500 ft, and 45 within 1,000 ft. The few dated use decisions nearby (N = 3 in the last 10 years within 1,000 ft, too few for a rate) show 2 approvals and 1 withdrawal, with most nearby restaurant and ABC referrals routinely approved as principally permitted uses in both the NCD-Lower Polk Street and adjacent RC-4 districts.

comparables.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 referral for a full-service restaurant 130 meters away in the same NCD-Lower Polk Street zoning district; approved February–March 2023.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral (Planning responding to ABC's zoning inquiry) approved Type 41 beer-and-wine license in 21 days as principally permitted in the NCD-Lower Polk Street district when operated as a bona fide eating place, subject to operating conditions in Planning Code §202.2(a)(1).

comparables.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 referral for a restaurant 69 meters away at 925 O'Farrell St in the RC-4 district, approved April 2018 as continuation of existing restaurant use.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved Type 41 license in 2 days at the nearest comparable address (925 O'Farrell) in the adjacent RC-4 district, confirming Type 41 is permitted with an existing restaurant use as a bona fide eating place per Planning Code §209.3.

comparables.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 referral at 655 Larkin St (137 meters away, RC-4 district) for continuation of existing restaurant use and license type, approved March 2019.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved Type 41 license in 11 days for a continuation of existing restaurant use in RC-4, adding a condition requiring compliance with Good Neighbor Policies per Planning Code §249.5(d)(6)—a standard requirement that may apply here.

comparables.why_comparable: Health Department referral for continuation of limited restaurant use at 731 Polk St (114 meters away) in the NCD-Lower Polk Street district, approved December 2020.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral for a limited restaurant (same cooking type as this concept) approved in 20 days in the NCD-Lower Polk Street district as principally permitted retail sales and service use per Planning Code §744, confirming the base restaurant use is not controversial.

comparables.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 referral at 810 Van Ness Ave (199 meters away, RC-4 district) for an existing restaurant, approved August–September 2019.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved Type 41 license in 19 days in conjunction with an existing restaurant use in RC-4 per Planning Code §209.3, showing consistent fast approval for beer-and-wine licenses added to operating restaurants in both districts.

comparables.why_comparable: Health referral for continuation of restaurant use at 700 Polk St (152 meters, RC-4 district), approved January 2019 subject to §202(a) operating conditions.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approved continuation of existing restaurant use in 10 days in RC-4, explicitly citing the standard eating/drinking use operating conditions of Planning Code §202(a), which apply to all food and beverage establishments.

comparables.why_comparable: Only use decision (Conditional Use Authorization) among the candidates: a formula-retail restaurant change of operator at 1000 Van Ness Ave (83 meters, RC-4 district), approved by Planning Commission July 2016.
comparables.key_takeaway: This Commission-level use decision took 93 days but was for a formula-retail change of operator (Ike's Love & Sandwiches replacing Quiznos), not a liquor license. It illustrates that discretionary hearings are required for formula retail, not for simple beer-and-wine licenses at non-chain restaurants.

comparables.why_comparable: Health Department referral for a limited restaurant at 709 Larkin St (114 meters, RC-4 district), filed March 2019 and approved September 2021.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral for a limited restaurant took 904 days to approve, but this extreme delay (likely COVID-era processing backlog, not opposition) is an outlier among the otherwise fast approvals and does not indicate use controversy.

patterns.pattern: ABC Type 41 (beer-and-wine, eating place) referrals for existing or continuation restaurant uses in both NCD-Lower Polk Street and RC-4 districts were routinely approved by Planning staff as principally permitted in 2–21 days, with no discretionary hearing required.
All ABC Type 41 approvals required the restaurant to operate as a 'Bona Fide Eating Place' under Planning Code §202.2, meaning food service is the primary use and alcohol is incidental to meals.

Planning applied standard location and operating conditions from Planning Code §202.2(a)(1) (or §202(a)) to eating and drinking uses, including requirements for hours, noise, litter control, and maintaining the food-service character.

At least one ABC Type 41 referral in the RC-4 district (655 Larkin St) added a condition requiring compliance with Good Neighbor Policies per Planning Code §249.5(d)(6), which may apply to intensifications of use in high-density residential areas.

Limited restaurant uses (same cooking type as this concept) were approved as principally permitted retail sales and service in both NCD-Lower Polk Street (§744) and RC-4 (§209.3) districts without discretionary review.

None of the agency referrals (the procedural path for an ABC zoning sign-off) went to a Planning Commission hearing; all were approved at staff level, contrasting with the 93-day Conditional Use Authorization required for formula retail.

The pathway rule lines state that a restaurant already exists at this address and continues, so the control for a new use was not applied and the intensification test was used instead; however, the records do not show what the space is used as.
No active ABC license of a type the rules read is on file at 895 O'Farrell St, so the records do not show what the space is used as now or whether a restaurant exists.
A new restaurant would be principally permitted here, so enlarging or intensifying an existing restaurant needs no Conditional Use under the intensification rule per Planning Code § 744.

Formula retail is a conditional use in the NCD-Lower Polk Street district per Planning Code § 744, but the description does not say whether the business is part of a chain, so the rules could not decide.

expected_conditions.condition: Must operate as a bona fide eating place: food service is the primary use and alcohol is incidental to meals, per Planning Code § 202.2.
expected_conditions.basis: All nearby ABC Type 41 approvals required bona fide eating place operation. Planning Code § 202.2 defines it: the restaurant must serve meals during all hours alcohol is served, and food sales must predominate over alcohol sales.

expected_conditions.condition: Subject to standard location and operating conditions for eating and drinking uses under Planning Code § 202.2(a)(1), including hours, noise, litter control, and maintaining food-service character.
expected_conditions.basis: Planning applied these standard operating conditions in the 2023 Type 41 approval at 1035 Geary St in the same NCD-Lower Polk Street district and in the 2019 continuation at 700 Polk St in RC-4.

expected_conditions.condition: May be required to comply with Good Neighbor Policies per Planning Code § 249.5(d)(6), including a plan to address noise, litter, loitering, and neighborhood concerns.
expected_conditions.basis: One ABC Type 41 referral at 655 Larkin St in the RC-4 district was conditioned on Good Neighbor Policies. This is more common in residential-adjacent locations or where intensification is proposed.

expected_conditions.condition: ABC Type 41 license (if beer-and-wine): minors are allowed on the premises, no service after 2 a.m., and a 30-day public posting at the premises during the application period.
expected_conditions.basis: The permit catalog entry for ABC Type 41 and state law set these standard conditions; protests during the posting period can trigger a Public Convenience or Necessity hearing.

expected_conditions.condition: If the space does not already have a commercial kitchen with hood and grease interceptor, installation of FOG control equipment per the SF Public Utilities Commission FOG ordinance will be required before opening.
expected_conditions.basis: The SF FOG ordinance requires every food service establishment that cooks to install grease-capturing equipment. The catalog entry notes that an undersized or missing interceptor is a common reason DBI withholds final sign-off.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm with the applicant whether the business is part of a chain (11+ locations), what type of alcohol will be served, and how the license will be obtained.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The rules could not decide on zoning and alcohol approvals without these answers. If the business is part of a chain, a Conditional Use Authorization hearing will be required for formula retail, adding 4–10 months and thousands in fees. If full liquor (Type 47 or 48), budget 6–12 months to locate, escrow and transfer a quota license at a high cost. If beer-and-wine only (Type 41), the license is non-quota and the path is much faster. Confirm these facts in writing before moving forward.

filing_playbook.action: Confirm with Planning in writing that a restaurant already exists at 895 O'Farrell St and that adding alcohol service is an intensification, not a new use.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The rules read that a restaurant continues at this address, but no ABC license or prior Planning application is on file to show it. Email Planning's Zoning Information Center or the front desk with the address, the lease, and a brief description (existing restaurant adding beer and wine) and ask whether this is a continuation of an existing restaurant use or a new restaurant use. If Planning says no restaurant exists, the concept will be treated as a new restaurant use, which is principally permitted but may trigger a change-of-use review by DBI and a Planning referral. Get the answer in writing before filing anything.

filing_playbook.action: Form the legal entity with the California Secretary of State, obtain an EIN from the IRS, and register the business with the SF Treasurer & Tax Collector.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File LLC Articles of Organization (Form LLC-1, $70) or corporation articles ($100) online at the CA Secretary of State. The same day, apply for an EIN at irs.gov (free, issued immediately). Within 30 days, register the business with SF Treasurer & Tax Collector for a Business Registration Certificate ($55–$700 based on gross receipts). The Business Account Number (BAN) from the city registration is required for every other city permit, so do this step early. If the business name differs from the legal entity name, file a Fictitious Business Name statement with the County Clerk and publish it in a newspaper within 45 days.

filing_playbook.action: Apply for a California Seller's Permit online with the CDTFA and arrange workers' compensation insurance.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The seller's permit is free and often issued the same day when you register online at cdtfa.ca.gov. ABC will not issue an alcohol license until the seller's permit exists, so get it before applying to ABC. Register as an employer with CA EDD within 15 days of hiring (free, online, 1–7 days). Arrange workers' compensation insurance with a licensed carrier or the State Fund (mandatory from the first employee); several city permits ask for proof of coverage.

filing_playbook.action: Have at least one owner or employee complete a Certified Food Protection Manager exam and have all food-handling employees obtain California Food Handler Cards.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: At least one person must pass an ANSI-accredited food safety certification exam (ServSafe, Prometric, etc., $100–$250, valid 5 years) within 60 days of opening; the health inspector will ask for the certificate at the pre-opening inspection. Every employee who handles food must obtain a Food Handler Card ($7–$15, online course takes ~2 hours, valid 3 years) within 30 days of hire. If the business will serve alcohol, every alcohol server and their managers must complete RBS (Responsible Beverage Service) training ($3 registration + $10–$25 course) within 60 days of hire; keep the certification list on site for ABC inspections.

filing_playbook.action: If tenant improvements or kitchen work are planned, or if no kitchen or grease interceptor exists, file a building permit application with DBI and route it to DPH for plan check.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: The description states no tenant improvements are planned, but if the space does not already have a commercial kitchen, hood, hand sinks, and grease interceptor that meet code, those installations will trigger a building permit and DPH plan check. Submit two sets of scaled plans, equipment layout, and menu to DPH via their online portal. DPH will route the building permit application to Planning for zoning sign-off. Schedule a pre-final inspection at ~80% complete and a final inspection at least two weeks before opening. If no kitchen work is needed, skip this step.

filing_playbook.action: Apply for a Health Permit to Operate online with DPH at least one month before opening, and schedule the pre-opening inspection.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply online at sfdph.org/ehsBizPortal with your BAN, Location ID (LIN), and federal tax ID. The $470 Permit to Operate application includes the initial inspection; the annual license fee for restaurants is $0 for FY2026–28. DPH will inspect to confirm the facility matches the approved plans, all equipment is in place, and a certified food safety manager is on staff. Schedule the inspection at least two weeks in advance. Common failures (missing hand sinks, unsealed surfaces, no hot water) push openings by 2–3 weeks, so walk the space against the DPH checklist before calling for the inspection.

filing_playbook.action: If beer-and-wine only (Type 41): apply to ABC for a Type 41 license online, post the public notice at the premises for 30 days, and submit the Planning and Police referral responses to ABC.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File the ABC-257 application online at abc.ca.gov with the signed lease, seller's permit, entity documents, and filing fee. ABC will mail you a notice to post at the premises for 30 days. Simultaneously, ABC will send referrals to SFPD and Planning; Planning's zoning sign-off for a Type 41 at a bona fide eating place in the NCD-Lower Polk Street district has been approved in 2–21 days in comparable cases. If no one protests during the 30-day posting and the census tract is not undue-concentration, expect ABC to issue the license in roughly 60–120 days from application. If the tract is high-crime or undue-concentration, ABC may require a Public Convenience or Necessity (PCN) letter from the city, adding time; confirm the tract status with ABC or SFPD before applying.

timeline_cost.notes: This range is the time and government cost to obtain a health permit to operate, the only approval the rules classified as allowed (no discretionary hearing required). The health permit is issued 14–45 days after application once the pre-opening inspection confirms the facility is ready, per the catalog entry. The $470–$1,000 range is the DPH Permit to Operate application fee including the initial inspection; the FY2026–27 annual license fee for restaurants is $0. This is a time to approval, not to denial or withdrawal. It does not include the ABC license, because the rules could not decide which ABC license type applies (the description does not state what alcohol will be served or how the license will be obtained). The building permit and change-of-use timeline is also excluded because the rules could not establish whether one is needed (the records do not show what the space was last used as, and the existing occupancy group is not in public records). The zoning and use row is insufficient information (formula retail not ruled out), so no discretionary hearing timeline is included here. State and federal business formation (EIN, entity registration, seller's permit, employer registration, insurance, food safety certifications, RBS training) add roughly 1–14 days and can be completed in parallel with city permits. Sign permit for exterior signage adds 7–45 days if new signage is installed. Music licenses (ASCAP, BMI) for recorded music add 1–7 days and should be set up in the final two weeks before opening. All day and cost figures are from the catalog entries cited.
